newsitem.title: USA: Swiss knew Nazi gold was looted - D'Amato.
newsitem.headline: Swiss knew Nazi gold was looted - D'Amato.

text.p: British, French and U.S. negotiators believed Switzerland knew how the gold it accepted from the Germans in the Second World War was obtained, according to a document released by U.S. Sen. Alfonse D'Amato on Sunday.
D'Amato said the Swiss took 100 tonnes of gold looted by the Nazis from Belgium. The New York senator said the document released on Sunday showed the Swiss were fully aware of what they had done.

The document, an April 17, 1946, report by the Allied Delegation called "Swiss Observations with Regard to the Gold Problem," said: "Switzerland cannot plead that she was ignorant of the despoilment and robbery which the Germans committed against the countries which were under her authority....
"It is the view of the Allied Delegations that Switzerland is responsible for all gold shipped to her from Germany," the document said.

"Documents show it was common knowledge during the war that the Germans did not legally own 100 tonnes of gold in 1943; that they had used up their pre-war supply of gold to pay for their war efforts," D'Amato said in remarks before 300 members of the Manhattan Beach Jewish Centre in the city's borough of Brooklyn.
"In this particular case, it was well known that the 100 tonnes, which was worth $123 million 50 years ago, would be worth well over a billion dollars in gold today," he said.

"That is not neutrality," he said, adding he intends to pursue the matter "to every last dollar. Half-truths and half distortions (by the Swiss) are not going to save the day. We want a full accounting."
The April 1946 report was written by Britain, France and U.S. negotiators during talks with Switzerland for the return of looted gold that the Nazis deposited in the neutral nation during the war.

However, D'Amato, U.S. Senate Banking Committee Chairman, wants the treaty re-negotiated because documents discovered in the U.S. National Archives show the Swiss received up to $400 million in gold from Germany.
